hints: Start with the top calibration image. Notice the 0 lines line up exactly, then look right to find the next place where a long eyepiece line lines up exactly with a long stage line.
Remember each small stage division is 0.01 mm. Work out what 30 eyepiece units equal in mm, then find the value of 1 eyepiece unit before you measure X to Y.
walkthrough:
**Calibrate the eyepiece graticule**

First, we must give the eyepiece units a real value using the stage micrometer. This calibration is only valid for this magnification.

Look for perfect alignment. The 0 lines align, and next the eyepiece 30 line aligns perfectly with the stage 0.2 mm line.

That means:
$$30 \text{ eyepiece units} = 0.2 \text{ mm}$$

**Calculate one eyepiece unit in micrometres**

One small stage division is $0.01 \text{ mm}$, so $0.2 \text{ mm}$ is 20 small divisions. Now divide to get one eyepiece unit.

$$1 \text{ eyepiece unit} = 0.2 \div 30 = 0.00667 \text{ mm}$$

Convert mm to micrometres by multiplying by 1000:
$$0.00667 \times 1000 = 6.67 \, \mu\text{m}$$

**Measure X to Y and convert to actual size**

Now look at the root photo. X is at about eyepiece 0 and Y is at about eyepiece 25.

$$\text{width in eyepiece units} = 25 - 0 = 25$$

Multiply by the calibrated value:
$$25 \times 6.67 \, \mu\text{m} = 166.7 \, \mu\text{m}$$

This rounds to about $170 \, \mu\text{m}$, which is option C.

options.A: Too small by a factor of 10. You have likely divided by 10 extra or mixed up mm and micrometres in the final conversion.
options.B: This is just the number of eyepiece units between X and Y. It forgets to calibrate the eyepiece against the stage micrometer.
options.C: Correct. 25 eyepiece units multiplied by about 6.67 micrometres per unit gives about 167 micrometres, closest to 170 micrometres.
options.D: Too large. This assumes 1 eyepiece unit equals 10 micrometres (one stage division), without using the correct 30 to 0.2 mm alignment.
